title: Large-output checkout incident and narrow rollback
initial_prompt: Read TASK.md. Investigate the checkout error spike using inputs/logs/day-01.jsonl and the current runtime configuration. Leave provisional structured findings and working notes. You can filter the source files or run node inputs/export.mjs; saving, redirecting, or repeating its output is allowed.

stages.message: Read TASK.md. Investigate the checkout error spike using inputs/logs/day-01.jsonl and the current runtime configuration. Leave provisional structured findings and working notes. You can filter the source files or run node inputs/export.mjs; saving, redirecting, or repeating its output is allowed.

The regional release catalog and gateway traces arrived. Determine which rollout changed behavior rather than blaming the nearest error in time. Keep the source event IDs, not just a prose summary. Do not edit configuration until the scope is established.

The upstream payment team supplied its independent traces. Join only same-region same-request events whose corrected UTC times differ by at most 120 seconds. A repeated request_id outside that interval is another request occurrence.

Clock calibration is now in inputs/clock-offsets.json. Each service clock equals UTC plus offset_ms; subtract the offset from raw_ms. Recompute first application error and first customer failure for the implicated release. Retain the raw source IDs.

Operations approved rolling back only the implicated region’s checkout timeout to the previous release value. Preserve every other JSON value, including independent emergency feature flags. Update config/runtime.json and the structured incident findings.

The archival replay includes a next-day occurrence of an already affected request ID and a same-time error in another region. Finalize output/incident.json. Exclude these unrelated occurrences; count the next-day occurrence under excluded_reused_request_count. Leave the narrow config rollback in place.
